title.en: Volume 294 Biographies 53: Zhang Yuxi, Su Shen, Wang Zhu, Xu Yan, Liu Zhi, Nie Guanqing, Feng Yuan, Zhao Shimin, Zhang Xi, Zhang Kui, Yang Anguo
title.raw: 卷二百九十四 列傳第五十三 掌禹錫 蘇紳 王洙 胥偃 柳植 聶冠卿 馮元 趙師民 張錫 張揆 楊安國 Volume 294 Biographies 53: Zhang Yuxi, Su Shen, Wang Zhu, Xu Yan, Liu Zhi, Nie Guanqing, Feng Yuan, Zhao Shimin, Zhang Xi, Zhang Kui, Yang Anguo

sentences.zh: 掌禹錫

translations.literal: Zhang Yuxi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuxi

sentences.zh: 掌禹錫，字唐卿，許州郾城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuxi, style name Tangqing, was a native of Yancheng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuxi, whose courtesy name was Tangqing, came from Yancheng in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，為道州司理參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial administrator in Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial aide in Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 試身言書判第一，改大理寺丞，累遷尚書屯田員外郎、通判幷州。

translations.literal: In the examination of physical bearing, speech, calligraphy, and legal judgment he ranked first; he was transferred to be an aide in the Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted repeatedly to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Revenue for State Farms and surveillance commissioner of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the examination of bearing, speech, calligraphy, and legal judgment, was made an aide in the Court of Judicial Review, and rose through several posts to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Revenue for State Farms and surveillance commissioner of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢知廬州，未行，丁度薦為侍御史，上疏請嚴備西羌。

translations.literal: He was selected to be prefect of Luzhou; before he took up the post, Ding Du recommended him as a censor, and he memorialized the throne urging strict preparations against the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen prefect of Luzhou, but before he departed Ding Du recommended him as a censor; he submitted a memorial urging thorough precautions against the Western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 時議舉兵，禹錫引周宣薄伐為得，漢武遠討為失；

translations.literal: When the court was debating whether to raise troops, Yu Xi cited King Xuan of Zhou's limited punitive campaign as the right course and Emperor Wu of Han's distant expedition as a mistake;
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated military action, Yu Xi argued that King Xuan of Zhou's restrained punitive campaign had been correct whereas Emperor Wu of Han's distant expedition had been a mistake;

sentences.zh: 且建畫增步卒，省騎兵。

translations.literal: and he proposed increasing infantry and reducing cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: and he proposed adding more foot soldiers while cutting back on cavalry.

sentences.zh: 舊法，薦舉邊吏，貪贓皆同坐。

translations.literal: Under the old law, when border officials were recommended, any who proved corrupt were punished along with their recommenders.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, anyone who recommended a border official was held jointly liable if that official proved corrupt.

sentences.zh: 禹錫奏謂：「使貪使愚，用兵之法也。

translations.literal: Yu Xi memorialized, saying: "To employ the greedy and employ the foolish—that is the method of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi submitted a memorial stating: "To use the greedy and to use the foolish—that is how one wages war.

sentences.zh: 若舉邊吏必兼責士節，則莫敢薦矣。

translations.literal: If in recommending border officials one must also hold them to standards of personal integrity, then no one will dare to recommend anyone.
translations.idiomatic: If every recommender of border officials must also answer for their moral character, no one will dare to put names forward.

sentences.zh: 材武者孰從而進哉？」

translations.literal: From whom, then, will men of martial talent advance?"
translations.idiomatic: How, then, will men of martial ability ever rise?"

sentences.zh: 後遂更其法。

translations.literal: Thereafter the law was changed.
translations.idiomatic: The regulation was eventually revised.

sentences.zh: 出提點河東刑獄。

translations.literal: He went out as judicial intendant of Hedong east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as judicial intendant for Hedong east of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 杜衍薦，召試，為集賢校理，改直集賢院兼崇文院檢討。

translations.literal: On Du Yan's recommendation he was summoned for examination and appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies; he was transferred to direct collator in that hall while also serving as reviser in the Chongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Du Yan, he was summoned for examination and made collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then direct collator in that hall with concurrent duty as reviser in the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷三司度支判官、判理欠司、同管勾國子監。

translations.literal: He successively served as fiscal affairs judge in the Three Departments, judge of outstanding debts, and co-superintendent of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as fiscal judge in the Three Departments, judge of outstanding debts, and co-superintendent of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 歷判司農、太常寺。

translations.literal: He also served as judge of the Ministry of Revenue and of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He also held judgeships in the Ministry of Revenue and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 數考試開封國學進士，命題皆奇奧，士子憚之，目為「難題掌公」。

translations.literal: Several times he set examination topics for jinshi candidates at the Directorate in Kaifeng; his questions were all abstruse, and the students feared him, calling him "Master Difficult Questions Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly set examination topics for jinshi candidates at the Kaifeng Directorate; his questions were uniformly recondite, and students so dreaded him that they nicknamed him "Master Difficult Questions Zhang."

sentences.zh: 遷光祿卿，改直秘閣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and transferred to direct collator in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and made direct collator in the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，自秘書監遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was moved from Director of the Palace Library to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, he was transferred from Director of the Palace Library to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 御史劾禹錫老病不任事，帝憐其博學多記，令召至中書，示以彈文。

translations.literal: The censorate impeached Yu Xi as old and ill and unfit for office; the emperor, pitying his vast learning and memory, had him summoned to the Secretariat and showed him the impeachment memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached Yu Xi on the grounds that age and illness left him unfit for duty; the emperor, taking pity on his wide learning and retentive memory, had him called to the Secretariat and showed him the impeachment text.

sentences.zh: 禹錫惶怖自請，遂以尚書工部侍郎致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Yu Xi, in fear and distress, asked to retire; he was therefore granted retirement as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi, terrified and ashamed, petitioned to retire and was allowed to leave office as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat; he then died.

sentences.zh: 禹錫矜慎畏法，居家勤儉，至自舉几案。

translations.literal: Yu Xi was proud, cautious, and law-fearing; at home he was industrious and frugal, even to the point of carrying his own tables and desks.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi was proud and scrupulous in observing the law; at home he lived frugally and diligently, even carrying his own tables and desks himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗預修《皇祐方域圖志》、《地理新書》，奏對帝前，王洙推其稽考有勞，賜三品服。

translations.literal: He once took part in compiling the Huangyou Gazetteer of the Realm and the New Book of Geography; when he answered before the throne, Wang Zhu commended his labor in textual verification, and he was granted third-rank court dress.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Huangyou Gazetteer of the Realm and the New Book of Geography; when he appeared before the emperor, Wang Zhu praised his painstaking research, and he was awarded third-rank ceremonial robes.

sentences.zh: 及校正《類篇》、《神農本草》，載藥石之名狀為《圖經》。

translations.literal: He also helped revise the Classified Lexicon and the Divine Farmer's Materia Medica, setting down the names and forms of drugs and stones in an illustrated treatise.
translations.idiomatic: He also assisted in correcting the Classified Lexicon and the Divine Farmer's Materia Medica, recording the names and descriptions of medicinals and minerals in an illustrated compendium.

sentences.zh: 喜命術，自推直生日，年庚寅，日乙酉，時壬午，當《易》之《歸妹》、《困》、《震》初中末三卦。

translations.literal: He delighted in fate-calculation arts. From his own straight-day birth date—year gengyin, day yiyou, hour renwu—he obtained the hexagrams Gui Mei, Kun, and Zhen of the Changes, in their initial, middle, and final lines respectively.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of divination. From his own birth date on the straight day—year gengyin, day yiyou, hour renwu—he derived the hexagrams Gui Mei, Kun, and Zhen from the Book of Changes, in their first, second, and third lines respectively.

sentences.zh: 以世應飛伏納五甲行軌析數推之，卦得二十五少分，三卦合七十五年約半，祿秩算數，盡於此矣。

translations.literal: Applying the methods of shifting the correspondent and the hidden lines, absorbing the five jia into the orbit, and analyzing numbers thereby, the hexagrams yielded twenty-five and a fractional part; the three hexagrams together indicated roughly seventy-five years and a half. His salary and rank were to be reckoned entirely within this span.
translations.idiomatic: By shifting correspondents and hidden lines, incorporating the five jia into the orbital cycle, and calculating the numbers, he obtained twenty-five and a fraction; the three hexagrams together pointed to about seventy-five and a half years. His stipend and office were, he concluded, fully accounted for within that span.

sentences.zh: 著《郡國手鑒》一卷，《周易集解》十卷。

translations.literal: He authored one fascicle of A Hand Mirror of Commanderies and States and ten fascicles of Collected Explanations of the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote one juan of A Hand Mirror of Commanderies and States and ten juan of Collected Explanations of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 好儲書，所記極博，然迂漫不能達其要。

translations.literal: He loved to hoard books and his memory was extremely broad, yet he was diffuse and could not grasp essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He loved collecting books and his memory was vast, yet he was discursive and never quite reached the heart of a subject.

sentences.zh: 常乘駑馬，衣冠汙垢，言語舉止多可笑，僚屬或慢侮之，過閭巷，人指以為戲云。

translations.literal: He habitually rode a poor horse, his hat and robes were soiled, and his speech and bearing were often laughable; subordinates sometimes treated him with contempt, and when he passed through lanes people would point at him in jest.
translations.idiomatic: He usually rode a sorry nag, wore stained hat and robes, and his words and manner were often ridiculous; colleagues sometimes slighted him, and in the streets people would point him out for amusement.

sentences.zh: 蘇紳，字儀甫，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Su Shen
translations.idiomatic: Su Shen

sentences.zh: 進士及第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 歷宜、復、安三州推官，改大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as investigating clerk in Yi, Fu, and An prefectures, and was transferred to be an aide in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as investigating clerk in Yi, Fu, and An prefectures, then was made an aide in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 母喪，寓揚州。

translations.literal: When his mother died he lodged in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he stayed in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 州將盛度以文學自負，見其文，大驚，自以為不及，由是知名。

translations.literal: The prefect Sheng Du, proud of his literary talent, was greatly startled when he saw Shen's writings and felt himself inferior; from this Shen became well known.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Sheng Du, who prided himself on his literary skill, was astonished by Shen's essays and judged himself Shen's inferior; from that time Shen's name spread.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士，舉賢良方正科，擢尚書祠部員外郎、通判洪州，徙揚州。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was recommended for the Exalted Worthies and Upright Scholars category, and was elevated to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Rites for Ancestral Temples and surveillance commissioner of Hongzhou; he was then transferred to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, entered the Exalted Worthies and Upright Scholars examination, and rose to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Rites for Ancestral Temples and surveillance commissioner of Hongzhou before being moved to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歸，上十議，進直史館，為開封府推官、三司鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: On his return he submitted ten policy proposals, was advanced to compiler in the Academy of History, and served as investigating official in the Kaifeng prefectural office and fiscal judge in the Salt and Iron Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he presented ten policy memorials, was promoted to compiler in the Academy of History, and served as investigating official in the Kaifeng prefectural office and fiscal judge in the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 時眾星西流，並代地大震，方春而雷，詔求直言，紳上疏極言時事。

translations.literal: At that time many stars moved westward, there was a great earthquake in Bing and Dai, and thunder sounded in spring; the throne sought forthright counsel, and Shen submitted a memorial speaking bluntly on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time numerous stars drifted westward, Bing and Dai suffered a major earthquake, and thunder rolled in spring; the emperor called for frank advice, and Shen submitted a memorial that spoke bluntly about affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 安化蠻蒙光月率眾寇宜州，敗官軍，殺鈐轄張懷志等六人。

translations.literal: Meng Guangyue of the Anhua barbarians led his followers to raid Yizhou, defeated government troops, and killed the deputy commander Zhang Huaizhi and five others.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guangyue of the Anhua tribes led his people in raiding Yizhou, routed the government army, and killed Deputy Commander Zhang Huaizhi and five other officers.

sentences.zh: 紳上言曰：

translations.literal: Shen memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shen submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 「國家比以西北二邊為意，而鮮復留意南方，故有今日之患，誠不可不慮也。

translations.literal: "The state has lately focused on the northwestern and northern frontiers and has scarcely attended to the south; hence today's calamity—this truly must not go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: "The court has lately been preoccupied with the northwestern and northern borders and has paid little heed to the south; that is why we face today's disaster, and this truly cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 臣頃從事宜州，粗知本末。

translations.literal: Your servant once served in Yizhou and has a rough knowledge of how matters stand.
translations.idiomatic: I once served in Yizhou and have some grasp of how matters stand there.

sentences.zh: 安化地幅員數百里，持兵之眾，不過三四千人。

translations.literal: Anhua territory extends several hundred li, and those bearing arms number no more than three or four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Anhua territory covers several hundred li, and men under arms number only three or four thousand at most.

sentences.zh: 然而敢肆侵擾，非特恃其險絕，亦由往者守將失計，而國家姑息之太過也。

translations.literal: Yet they dare to commit aggression—not only because they rely on rugged terrain, but also because former border commanders miscalculated and the state has indulged them too far.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they dare raid the borders—not only because the terrain is forbidding, but also because past commanders erred and the court has been too indulgent.

sentences.zh: 向聞宜州吏民言，祥符中，蠻人騷動，朝廷興兵討伐。

translations.literal: I have heard the officials and people of Yizhou say that in the Xiangfu era the barbarians stirred and the court raised troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people in Yizhou say that during the Xiangfu period the tribes rebelled and the court sent troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 是時，唯安撫都監馬玉勒兵深入，多殺所獲。

translations.literal: At that time only the pacification commissioner and military inspector Ma Yu led troops deep in and killed many captives.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only Pacification Commissioner and Military Inspector Ma Yu drove deep into their territory and killed many captives.

sentences.zh: 知桂州曹克明害其功，累移文止之，故玉志不得逞。

translations.literal: The prefect of Guizhou, Cao Keming, envied his achievement and repeatedly sent documents to stop him, so Yu's plans could not be carried through.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Keming, prefect of Guizhou, jealous of his success, sent repeated dispatches to halt him, so Yu could not finish what he had begun.

sentences.zh: 蠻人畏伏其名，至今言者猶惜之。

translations.literal: The barbarians feared and submitted to his name, and even now those who speak of it still regret what happened.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes feared his reputation, and even today people still lament that he was not allowed to prevail.

sentences.zh: 使當時領兵者皆如玉，則蠻當殄滅，無今日之患矣。

translations.literal: If all who led troops then had been like Yu, the barbarians would have been exterminated and there would be no trouble today.
translations.idiomatic: Had every commander then been like Ma Yu, the tribes would have been wiped out and we would have no trouble today.

sentences.zh: 至使乘隙蹂邊，屠殺將吏，其損國威，無甚於此。

translations.literal: As it is, they seized the opportunity to trample the frontier and slaughter officers—nothing has damaged national prestige more than this.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they seized the moment to ravage the border and slaughter officers—nothing has done more harm to the dynasty's prestige.

sentences.zh: 朝廷儻不以此時加兵，則無以創艾將來，而震疊荒裔。

translations.literal: If the court does not send troops at this juncture, there will be no way to chastise the future or to awe the distant tribes.
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not use force now, we cannot chastise future rebels or overawe the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 彼六臣者，雖不善為馭，自致喪敗，然銜冤負恥，當有以刷除。

translations.literal: Those six officers, though poor commanders who brought defeat on themselves, yet died bearing grievance and shame; they deserve to have that stain wiped away.
translations.idiomatic: Those six officers were poor leaders and brought defeat on themselves, yet they died disgraced and wronged; their honor should be restored.

sentences.zh: 臣觀蠻情，所恃者地形險阨，據高臨下，大軍難以並進。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that the barbarians rely on rugged terrain, holding the heights and looking down, so large armies cannot advance together.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes rely on steep ground, holding the heights and looking down, so large forces cannot advance in a body.

sentences.zh: 然其壤土磽確，資蓄虛乏，刀耕火種，以為餱糧。

translations.literal: Yet their soil is poor and thin, their stores meager; they till with knife and burn for food.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their land is barren, their stores scant; they farm by slash-and-burn and live hand to mouth.

sentences.zh: 其勢可以緩圖，不可以速取；

translations.literal: Their situation may be taken slowly, not seized quickly;
translations.idiomatic: They can be worn down slowly, not crushed at a stroke;

sentences.zh: 可以計覆，不可以力爭。

translations.literal: they may be overcome by stratagem, not by brute force.
translations.idiomatic: they can be overcome by strategy, not by frontal assault.

sentences.zh: 今廣東西教閱忠敢澄海、湖南北雄武等軍，皆慣涉險阻。

translations.literal: Now the Chenghai and Xiongwu armies of Guangdong and Guangxi and of Hunan, trained for loyalty and daring, are all practiced in hazardous terrain.
translations.idiomatic: The Chenghai and Xiongwu regiments of Guangdong, Guangxi, Hunan, and Hubei, drilled for loyalty and courage, are all accustomed to difficult country.

sentences.zh: 又所習兵器，與蠻人略同。

translations.literal: Moreover the weapons they train with are much the same as those of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Their weapons, moreover, closely resemble those of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 請速發詣宜州策應，而以他兵代之。

translations.literal: I ask that they be sent quickly to Yizhou to support operations, and that other troops replace them.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that these units be dispatched at once to Yizhou to support operations while other troops relieve them.

sentences.zh: 仍命轉運使備數年軍食，今秋、冬之交，嵐氣已息，進軍據其出路，轉粟補卒，為曠日持久之計。

translations.literal: Also order the transport commissioners to prepare several years' grain for the army; in the interval between autumn and winter, when miasma has abated, advance and hold their exit routes, rotate grain and reinforcements, and plan for a prolonged campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Let transport officials stock several years' provisions; when autumn miasma lifts, advance to block their escape routes, rotate grain and fresh troops, and plan a long campaign.

sentences.zh: 伺得便利，即圖深入，可以傾蕩巢穴，杜絕蹊逕。

translations.literal: When a favorable opportunity appears, strike deep at once to overturn their nests and cut off their paths.
translations.idiomatic: When opportunity offers, drive deep to destroy their strongholds and seal their mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 縱使奔迸林莽，亦且壞其室廬，焚其積聚，使進無鈔略之獲，退無攻守之備。

translations.literal: Even if they flee into forest and thicket, destroy their dwellings and burn their stores so that advancing brings no booty and retreat leaves no base for attack or defense.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they scatter into the woods, ruin their houses and burn their grain so that advance yields no plunder and retreat offers no refuge.

sentences.zh: 然後諭以國恩，許以送款，而徙之內郡，收其土地，募民耕種，異時足以拓外夷為屏蔽也。

translations.literal: Then proclaim imperial grace, promise them surrender if they submit, move them into inner commanderies, reclaim their land, recruit settlers to farm it, and in time this will extend the frontier and serve as a barrier against outer tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Then proclaim the court's mercy, offer terms if they surrender, relocate them to interior prefectures, reclaim their land, and settle farmers on it—over time this will extend the frontier and shield the empire from outer tribes.

sentences.zh: 仍詔旁近諸蠻，諭以朝廷討叛之意，毋得相為聲援；

translations.literal: Also instruct neighboring tribes of the court's purpose in punishing rebellion and forbid them to lend support;
translations.idiomatic: Also instruct neighboring tribes that the court is punishing rebellion and that they must not aid the rebels;

sentences.zh: 如獲首級，即優賞以金帛。

translations.literal: if they present enemy heads, reward them generously with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: reward with gold and silk anyone who brings in enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 計若出此，則不越一年，逆寇必就殄滅。

translations.literal: If this plan is adopted, within a year the rebels will surely be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt this plan and within a year the rebels should be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 況廣西溪峒、荊湖、川峽蠻落甚多，大抵好為騷動。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the streams and ravines of western Guang, Jinghu, and the Sichuan gorges there are many tribal settlements, most of whom are prone to disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the streams of western Guang, the Jinghu region, and the Sichuan gorges there are many tribal settlements, most inclined to unrest.

sentences.zh: 因此一役，必皆震讋，可保數十年無俶擾之虞矣。」

translations.literal: By this one campaign they will all be awed and for several decades we may be free from the worry of sudden raids."
translations.idiomatic: One such campaign will awe them all and secure decades without sudden raids."

sentences.zh: 朝廷施用其策，遣馮伸己守桂州經制之，蠻遂平。

translations.literal: The court adopted his plan, sent Feng Shenji to hold Guizhou and direct operations, and the barbarians were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his advice, sent Feng Shenji to Guizhou to direct operations, and the tribes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 又陳便宜八事：

translations.literal: He also set forth eight measures of practical benefit:
translations.idiomatic: He also presented eight practical reforms:

sentences.zh: 「一曰重爵賞。

translations.literal: "First, value ranks and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: "First, hold ranks and rewards in esteem.

sentences.zh: 先王爵以褒德，祿以賞功，名以定流品，位以居才實。

translations.literal: The ancient kings used nobility to honor virtue, stipends to reward merit, names to fix social grades, and posts to seat men of real talent.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings used titles to honor virtue, stipends to reward merit, names to fix social standing, and offices to seat men of real ability.

sentences.zh: 未有無德而據高爵，無功而食厚祿，非其人而受美名，非其才而在顯位者。

translations.literal: Never did the undeserving hold high rank, the unmeritorious enjoy thick stipends, the unworthy receive fine names, or the incapable occupy eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Never did the undeserving hold high rank, the unmeritorious enjoy rich stipends, the unworthy win fine reputations, or the incapable fill eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 不妄與人官，非惜寵也，蓋官非其人，則不肖者逞。

translations.literal: Not to give office rashly is not stinginess with favor; if the office is not suited to the man, the unworthy will prevail.
translations.idiomatic: To withhold office is not miserliness; when office goes to the wrong man, the unworthy prevail.

sentences.zh: 不妄賞人，非愛財也，蓋實非其人，則徼幸者眾。

translations.literal: Not to reward rashly is not love of wealth; if the reward is not suited to the deed, the opportunistic will multiply.
translations.idiomatic: To withhold rewards is not love of money; when rewards miss their mark, opportunists multiply.

sentences.zh: 非特如此而已，則又敗國傷政，納侮詒患。

translations.literal: It is not only that: it also ruins the state, harms government, invites contempt, and breeds disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, it ruins the state, corrupts government, invites contempt, and breeds calamity.

sentences.zh: 上干天氣，下戾人心，災異既興，妖孽乃見。

translations.literal: Above it offends Heaven's qi; below it alienates men's hearts; prodigies arise and portents appear.
translations.idiomatic: Above it offends Heaven's harmony; below it alienates the people; omens and portents follow.

sentences.zh: 故漢世五侯同日封，天氣赤黃，及丁、傅封而其變亦然。

translations.literal: Thus in Han, when five marquises were enfeoffed on the same day the weather turned red and yellow; when Ding and Fu were enfeoffed the same anomaly occurred.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, when five marquises were enfeoffed on one day the sky turned red and yellow; when Ding and Fu were enfeoffed the same omen appeared.

sentences.zh: 楊宣以為爵土過制，傷亂土氣之祥也。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan held that excessive enfeoffment and grants of territory were an omen of harm to the soil's qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan held that excessive titles and land grants disturbed the qi of the realm.

sentences.zh: 二曰慎選擇。

translations.literal: Second, be careful in selection.
translations.idiomatic: "Second, be careful in selection.

sentences.zh: 今內外之臣，序年遷改，以為官濫，而復有論述微效，援此希進者。

translations.literal: Today inner and outer officials advance by seniority alone, as if office were cheap, while some also cite minor achievements in memorials hoping for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Today officials within and without the capital advance chiefly by seniority, as though office were cheap, while others cite minor achievements in memorials hoping to rise.

sentences.zh: 朝臣則有升監司，使臣則有授橫行。

translations.literal: Court officials may be raised to surveillance commissioners; envoys may be given lateral commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials are promoted to surveillance posts; commissioners receive extraordinary commissions.

sentences.zh: 不問人材物望，可與不可，並甄錄之。

translations.literal: Without asking talent, reputation, or fitness, all are enrolled alike.
translations.idiomatic: Without regard to talent, reputation, or fitness, all are enrolled alike.

sentences.zh: 不三數年，坐致清顯。

translations.literal: In fewer than three years they sit in eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years they reach eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 如此不止，則異日必以將相為賞矣。

translations.literal: If this continues, in time even generals and chancellors will be given as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Carried further, even generals and chancellors will be handed out as rewards.

sentences.zh: 三曰明薦舉。

translations.literal: Third, clarify recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: "Third, clarify recommendations.

sentences.zh: 今有位多援親舊，或迫於權貴，甚非薦賢助國，為官擇人之道。

translations.literal: Today many in office recommend kin, or are pressed by the powerful—far from the way of recommending the worthy to aid the state and choosing men for office.
translations.idiomatic: Too many in office recommend relatives or bow to the powerful—far from recommending the worthy to aid the state and choosing men fit for office.

sentences.zh: 若要官闕人，宜如祖宗故事，取班簿親擇五品以上清望官，各令舉一二人，述其才能德業，陛下與執政大臣，參驗而擢之。

translations.literal: When offices lack men, follow the ancestral practice: take the roster and have eminent fifth-rank officials each recommend one or two men, stating their ability and conduct; the throne and chief ministers should verify and appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: When offices stand vacant, follow ancestral practice: from the roster choose eminent fifth-rank officials, each to recommend one or two men with a statement of ability and conduct; the emperor and chief ministers should verify and appoint.

sentences.zh: 試而有效，則先賞舉者，否則黜責之。

translations.literal: If trial proves effective, reward the recommender first; if not, demote and punish him.
translations.idiomatic: If the appointee succeeds, reward the recommender first; if not, demote and punish him.

sentences.zh: 如此，則人人得以自勸。

translations.literal: Thus everyone will be able to urge himself on.
translations.idiomatic: Then everyone will strive to recommend well.

sentences.zh: 又選人條約太嚴。

translations.literal: Moreover the regulations for selecting officials are too strict.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the rules for selecting officials have grown too strict.

sentences.zh: 舊制，三人保者，得選京官，今則五人。

translations.literal: Formerly three guarantors sufficed for selection to capital office; now five are required.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly three guarantors sufficed for promotion to capital office; now five are required.

sentences.zh: 舊轉運使、提點刑獄率當三人，今止當一人。

translations.literal: Formerly transport commissioners and judicial intendants each counted for three guarantors; now only one counts.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly transport commissioners and judicial intendants each counted as three guarantors; now only one counts.

sentences.zh: 舊大兩省官歲舉五人，今才舉三人；

translations.literal: Formerly senior officials in the two inner secretariats recommended five men each year; now only three;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly senior officials in the two inner secretariats recommended five men a year; now only three;

sentences.zh: 升朝官舉三人，今則舉一人。

translations.literal: officials above court audience recommended three; now only one.
translations.idiomatic: officials above court audience recommended three; now only one.

sentences.zh: 舊不以在任及所統屬皆得奏舉，今則須在任及統屬方許論薦。

translations.literal: Formerly one was not required to be in office or within one's jurisdiction to recommend; now one must be in office and within jurisdiction to recommend.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly one need not be in office or within one's jurisdiction to recommend; now one must be in office and within one's chain of command.

sentences.zh: 驅馳下僚，未免有賢愚同滯之歎也。

translations.literal: Lower officials driven on in this way cannot but lament that worthy and unworthy are stalled alike.
translations.idiomatic: Lower officials cannot but lament that worthy and unworthy alike are left stuck.

sentences.zh: 四曰異服章。

translations.literal: Fourth, differentiate insignia.
translations.idiomatic: "Fourth, differentiate insignia.

sentences.zh: 朝班中執技之人與丞郎清望同佩金魚，內侍班行與學士同服金帶，豈朝廷待賢才、加禮遇之意？

translations.literal: In court ranks, men who perform technical duties wear the golden fish alongside vice directors and directors of clear reputation; in the inner service, attendants wear the golden belt like academicians—is this how the court honors talent and shows courtesy?
translations.idiomatic: In court ranks, technical specialists wear the golden fish alongside vice directors of clear reputation; inner attendants wear the golden belt like Hanlin academicians—is this how the court honors talent and shows distinction?

sentences.zh: 宜加裁定，使采章有別，則人品定而朝儀正矣。

translations.literal: Regulations should be drawn up so that insignia differ; then men's standing will be fixed and court ritual will be correct.
translations.idiomatic: Draw up regulations so insignia differ; then rank will be clear and court ritual restored.

sentences.zh: 五曰適才宜。

translations.literal: Fifth, match talent to task.
translations.idiomatic: "Fifth, match talent to task.

sentences.zh: 古者自黃、散而下，及隋之六品，唐之五品，皆吏部得專去留。

translations.literal: In antiquity, from Yellow Gate Attendants and Scattered Officials downward, and in Sui's sixth rank and Tang's fifth rank, the Ministry of Personnel alone decided retention and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, from Yellow Gate attendants and scattered officials downward, and through Sui's sixth rank and Tang's fifth rank, the Ministry of Personnel alone decided who stayed and who went.

sentences.zh: 今審官院、流內銓，則古之吏部；

translations.literal: Today's Court for Review of Appointments and the Inner Circulation Board are the ancient Ministry of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: Today's Court for Review of Appointments and the Inner Circulation Board are the old Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 三班院，古之兵部。

translations.literal: the Three-Rank Court is the ancient Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: the Three-Rank Court is the old Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 不問官職之閑劇，才能之長短，惟以資歷深淺為先後，有司但主簿籍而已。

translations.literal: Without asking whether posts are light or heavy or whether talent is long or short, precedence goes solely to depth of seniority; the offices merely keep the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Without regard to whether a post is important or minor or whether talent is great or small, promotion follows seniority alone; the bureaus merely maintain the registers.

sentences.zh: 欲賢不肖有別，不可得也。

translations.literal: To wish worthy and unworthy to be distinguished is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To distinguish the worthy from the unworthy is impossible under such a system.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝始用趙普議，置考課院以分中書之權，今審官是也，其職任豈輕也哉？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong first adopted Zhao Pu's proposal and established the Bureau of Performance Review to divide the Secretariat's power—today's Court for Review is that office; can its duty be considered light?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong first followed Zhao Pu's advice and set up the Bureau of Performance Review to divide the Secretariat's authority—the present Court for Review is that office; its responsibility can hardly be called slight.

sentences.zh: 宜擇主判官，付之以事權，責成其選事。

translations.literal: The chief reviewing official should be carefully chosen, entrusted with authority, and held responsible for selections.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the presiding reviewer with care, give him real authority, and hold him accountable for appointments.

sentences.zh: 若以為格例之設久，不可遽更。

translations.literal: If one holds that precedent has long stood and cannot be changed abruptly,
translations.idiomatic: If one holds that precedent is too entrenched to change overnight,

sentences.zh: 或有異才高行，許別論奏，如寇準判銓，薦選人錢若水等三人，並遷朝官為直館。

translations.literal: men of exceptional talent and high conduct should be allowed separate memorials, as when Kou Zhun judged the board and recommended three candidates including Qian Ruoshui, all of whom were promoted to court office and direct appointment in the academies.
translations.idiomatic: allow men of exceptional talent and conduct to be recommended by special memorial, as when Kou Zhun judged the board and advanced three candidates including Qian Ruoshui, all promoted to court office and direct academy posts.

sentences.zh: 其非才亦許奏殿，如唐盧從願為吏部，非才實者並令罷選，十不取一是也。

translations.literal: The unworthy should also be allowed memorials to the throne, as when Tang's Lu Congyuan was in the Ministry of Personnel and had the unworthy dismissed from candidacy, taking only one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: the unworthy should likewise be reported to the throne, as when Tang's Lu Congyuan in the Ministry of Personnel dismissed unfit candidates, accepting only one in ten.

sentences.zh: 六曰擇將帥。

translations.literal: Sixth, choose generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: "Sixth, choose generals and commanders.

sentences.zh: 漢制邊防有警，左右之臣，皆將帥也。

translations.literal: Under Han institutions, when the frontier was alarmed, ministers at the ruler's side were all generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han practice, when the frontier was threatened, the emperor's close ministers were themselves generals and commanders.

sentences.zh: 唐室文臣，自員外、郎中以上，為刺史、團練、防禦、觀察、節度等使，皆是養將帥之道，豈嘗限以文武？

translations.literal: In Tang, civil officials from outer-court vice-directors and directors upward served as prefects, training commissioners, defense commissioners, surveillance commissioners, and military commissioners—all ways of nurturing commanders; were they ever limited to civil or military tracks?
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, civil officials from vice-director and director upward served as prefects, training commissioners, defense commissioners, surveillance commissioners, and military commissioners—all ways of training commanders; were civil and military ever rigidly separated?

sentences.zh: 比年設武舉，所得人不過授以三班官，使人監臨，欲圖其建功立事，何可得也？

translations.literal: In recent years the military examination has been established, yet those obtained are only given Three-Rank posts and made to supervise—how can one expect them to achieve merit and establish deeds?
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the military examination has been instituted, yet graduates receive only Three-Rank posts and supervisory duties—how can they be expected to win distinction in the field?

sentences.zh: 臣僚舉換右職者，必人才弓馬兼書算策略，亦責之太備。

translations.literal: When ministers recommend transfer to military posts, they require talent in bow, horse, writing, calculation, and strategy—too demanding altogether.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers recommend men for military posts they demand mastery of bow, horse, writing, calculation, and strategy—demands far too strict.

sentences.zh: 宜使有材武者居統領之任，有謀畫者任邊防之寄，士若素養之，不慮不為用也。

translations.literal: Men of martial talent should hold command, men of stratagem should bear frontier responsibility; if scholars are nurtured, one need not fear they will not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Let men of martial talent hold command and men of stratagem bear frontier responsibility; cultivate talent properly and it will serve the state.

sentences.zh: 七曰辨忠邪。

translations.literal: Seventh, distinguish loyal from depraved.
translations.idiomatic: "Seventh, distinguish loyal from depraved.

sentences.zh: 夫忠賢之嫉姦邪，謂之去惡，惡不去則害政而傷國。

translations.literal: When the loyal and worthy hate the depraved, it is called removing evil; if evil is not removed, government is harmed and the state injured.
translations.idiomatic: When loyal men hate the wicked, they remove evil; if evil is not removed, government suffers and the state is harmed.

sentences.zh: 姦邪陷忠良，謂之蔽明，明不蔽，則無以稔其慝而肆其毒矣。

translations.literal: When the depraved entrap the loyal, it is called obscuring clarity; if clarity is not obscured, they cannot deepen their wickedness and unleash their poison.
translations.idiomatic: When the wicked entrap the loyal, they obscure judgment; if judgment stays clear, villains cannot deepen their plots and spread their poison.

sentences.zh: 忠邪之端，惟人主深辨之。

translations.literal: The distinction between loyal and depraved depends solely on the ruler's deep discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Only the ruler's keen discernment can tell loyal from depraved.

sentences.zh: 自古稱帝之聖者，莫如唐堯，然而四凶在朝，圮毀善類。

translations.literal: Of all called sage emperors, none surpasses Tang Yao, yet the Four Evils were in court and destroyed good men.
translations.idiomatic: Of all called sage rulers, none surpasses Tang Yao, yet the Four Evils sat in court and ruined good men.

sentences.zh: 好賢之甚者，莫如漢文，然而絳、灌在列，不容賢臣。

translations.literal: Of those who loved the worthy most, none surpasses Han Wendi, yet Zhou Bo and Guan Ying were in the ranks and would not tolerate worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who loved worthy men most, none surpasses Emperor Wen of Han, yet Zhou Bo and Guan Ying in office would not tolerate worthy ministers.

sentences.zh: 願監此而不使譽毀之說得行，愛憎之徒逞志，則忠賢進而邪慝消矣。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty heed this and not let praise and slander run free or partisans of love and hate have their way; then the loyal and worthy will advance and the depraved will fade.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty heed this lesson: do not let flattery and slander prevail or partisans of favor and spite have their way; then loyal men will rise and villains fade.

sentences.zh: 八曰修預備。

translations.literal: Eighth, repair preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: "Eighth, repair preparedness.

sentences.zh: 國家承平，天下無事將八十載，民食宜足而不足，國用宜豐而未豐，甚可怪也。

translations.literal: The state has enjoyed peace and the realm has been without major war for nearly eighty years, yet the people's food should be ample and is not, state revenue should be abundant and is not—how strange.
translations.idiomatic: The state has known peace and the realm has been largely free of war for nearly eighty years, yet the people's food should be ample and is not, state revenue should be rich and is not—how strange.

sentences.zh: 往者明道初，蟲螟水旱，幾遍天下。

translations.literal: In the early Mingdao era locusts, floods, and drought spread almost across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Mingdao era locusts, floods, and drought spread across nearly the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 始之以饑饉，繼之以疾疫，民之轉流死亡，不可勝數。

translations.literal: First came famine, then pestilence; the people who drifted away and died are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Famine came first, then pestilence; the people who fled and died are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 幸而比年稍稔，流亡稍復，而在位未嘗留意於備預之道，莫若安民而厚利，富國而足食。

translations.literal: Fortunately harvests have been somewhat better in recent years and refugees have partly returned, yet those in office have never attended to preparedness—nothing is better than settling the people and enriching profit, enriching the state and filling granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately harvests have improved somewhat and refugees have partly returned, yet those in office have never attended to preparedness—nothing surpasses settling the people and enriching them, enriching the state and filling its granaries.

sentences.zh: 欲民之安，則不之擇守宰、明教化；

translations.literal: To settle the people, choose prefects and magistrates and clarify instruction;
translations.idiomatic: To settle the people, choose good prefects and magistrates and clarify moral instruction;

sentences.zh: 欲民之利，則為之去兼並、禁遊末。

translations.literal: to enrich the people, remove land consolidation and forbid idle pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: to enrich the people, curb land concentration and forbid idle trades.

sentences.zh: 恤其疾苦，寬其徭役，則民安而利矣。

translations.literal: Relieve their hardships and lighten their corvée, and the people will be settled and enriched.
translations.idiomatic: Relieve their hardships and lighten their labor levies, and the people will be settled and prosper.

sentences.zh: 欲國之富，則必崇節儉，敦質素，蠲浮費。

translations.literal: To enrich the state, esteem frugality, encourage simplicity, and cut wasteful spending.
translations.idiomatic: To enrich the state, honor frugality, encourage simplicity, and cut wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 欲食之足，則省官吏之冗，去兵釋之蠹，絕奢靡之弊，塞凋偽之原，則國食足矣。

translations.literal: To fill granaries, reduce redundant officials, remove the bane of released soldiers, end extravagant abuses, and block the sources of false display, and state grain will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: To fill granaries, cut redundant officials, end abuses in demobilized troops, stop extravagant waste, and seal off sham display, and state grain will suffice.

sentences.zh: 民足於下，國富於上，雖有災沴，不足憂也。」

translations.literal: When the people below are full and the state above is rich, even if disaster strikes there is little to fear."
translations.idiomatic: When the people below are secure and the state above is rich, even disaster need not be feared."

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 進史館修撰，擢知制誥，入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to compiler in the Academy of History, elevated to drafter of edicts, and entered the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compiler in the Academy of History, made drafter of edicts, and entered the Hanlin Academy as academician.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 王素、歐陽修為諫官，數言事，紳忌之。

translations.literal: Wang Su and Ouyang Xiu served as remonstrance officials and spoke often on affairs; Shen resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su and Ouyang Xiu served as remonstrance officials and spoke often on policy; Shen resented them.

sentences.zh: 會京師閔雨，紳請對，言：「《洪範》五事，『言之不從，是謂不乂，厥咎僭，厥罰常暘。』

translations.literal: When the capital held rain prayers for drought, Shen requested audience and said: "In the Great Plan's five affairs, 'when words are not followed, this is called disorder; its blame is presumption, its punishment constant drought.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital prayed for rain during drought, Shen requested audience and said: "In the Great Plan's five affairs, 'when words are not followed, this is disorder; the blame is presumption, the punishment constant drought.

sentences.zh: 蓋言國之號令，不專於上，威福之柄，或移臣下，虛嘩憤亂，故其咎僭。」

translations.literal: This means the state's orders are not concentrated above, the handle of authority and favor sometimes shifts to ministers, and clamor and disorder arise—hence the blame of presumption."
translations.idiomatic: This means state orders are not concentrated at the top, authority and favor sometimes shift to ministers, and clamor and disorder arise—hence the blame of presumption."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「庶位逾節茲謂僭。

translations.literal: He also said: "When subordinate posts overstep their bounds, this is called presumption.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When subordinate posts overstep their bounds, this is presumption.

sentences.zh: 刑賞妄加，群陰不附，則陽氣勝，故其罰常暘。

translations.literal: When punishments and rewards are rashly applied, yin forces do not attach, then yang prevails—hence the punishment of constant drought.
translations.idiomatic: When punishments and rewards are rashly applied, yin forces do not attach and yang prevails—hence the punishment of constant drought.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷號令，有不一者，庶位有逾節而陵上者，刑賞有妄加於下者，下人有謀而僭上者。

translations.literal: Today court orders are not uniform; some subordinates overstep and insult superiors; punishments and rewards are rashly applied below; and inferiors plot presumption against superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Today court orders are not uniform; some subordinates overstep and insult superiors; punishments and rewards are rashly applied below; and inferiors plot against their betters.

sentences.zh: 此而不思，雖禱於上下神祇，殆非天意。」

translations.literal: If this is not pondered, though one pray to spirits above and below, it will scarcely accord with Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: If this is not pondered, prayer to spirits above and below will scarcely accord with Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 紳意以指諫官。

translations.literal: Shen's intent was to point at the remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's intent was to strike at the remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 諫官亦言紳舉御史馬端非其人，改龍圖閣學士、知揚州，復為翰林學士、史館修撰、權判尚書省。

translations.literal: The remonstrance officials also said Shen had recommended the censor Ma Duan, who was unfit; he was transferred to academician in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Yangzhou, then restored as Hanlin academician, Academy compiler, and acting head of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officials also charged that Shen had recommended the unfit censor Ma Duan; he was transferred to academician in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and prefect of Yangzhou, then restored as Hanlin academician, Academy compiler, and acting head of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 紳銳於進取，善中傷人。

translations.literal: Shen was keen to advance and skilled at striking others down.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was ambitious and skilled at undermining others.

sentences.zh: 陰中王德用，其疏至有「宅枕乾岡，貌類藝祖」之語，帝惡之，匿其疏不下。

translations.literal: He secretly attacked Wang Dezhi; his memorial even said "his residence lies on the Qian ridge, his appearance resembles Founder Taizu"—the emperor detested it and suppressed the memorial without publishing it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly attacked Wang Dezhi; his memorial even said "his residence lies on the Qian ridge, his appearance resembles Founder Taizu"—the emperor detested it and suppressed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 遂出紳，以吏部郎中改侍讀學士、集賢殿修撰、知河陽，徙河中。

translations.literal: Shen was therefore sent out, changed from director in the Ministry of Personnel to reader-in-waiting and compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was therefore sent out, moved from director in the Ministry of Personnel to reader-in-waiting and compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Heyang, then transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 未行感疾，為醫者藥所誤，猶力疾笞之，已而卒。

translations.literal: Before he departed he fell ill; a physician's medicine harmed him, yet he still forced himself to flog the doctor, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed he fell ill; a physician's medicine harmed him, yet he still forced himself to flog the doctor, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 紳博學多知，喜言事。

translations.literal: Shen was broadly learned and fond of speaking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was broadly learned and fond of policy debate.

sentences.zh: 嘗請罷連日視朝，復唐制朔望喚仗入閣，間開便殿，延對輔臣；

translations.literal: He once asked to end consecutive days of court audience, restore Tang practice of calling the guard on the first and fifteenth to enter the hall, occasionally open the informal hall, and extend audience to chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: He once asked to end consecutive days of court audience, restore Tang practice of summoning the guard on the first and fifteenth to enter the hall, occasionally open the informal hall, and extend audience to chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 寬制舉科格，以收才傑；

translations.literal: broaden examination regulations to gather outstanding talent;
translations.idiomatic: broaden examination regulations to gather outstanding talent;

sentences.zh: 選命諫員，勿侵御史職事。

translations.literal: and in selecting remonstrance officials, not let them encroach on censorial duties.
translations.idiomatic: and in selecting remonstrance officials, not let them encroach on censorial duties.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊反，請詔邊帥為入討之計，且曰：「以十年防守之費，為一歲攻取之資；

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, he asked that frontier commanders be ordered to plan invasion, and said: "Take ten years' cost of defense as one year's cost of attack;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, he asked that frontier commanders plan invasion, saying: "Take ten years' cost of defense as one year's cost of attack;

sentences.zh: 不爾，則防守之備，不止於十年矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise defense will cost more than ten years."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise defense will cost more than ten years."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今邊兵止備陝西，恐賊出不意窺河東，即麟、府不可不慮，宜稍移兵備之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Today frontier troops guard only Shaanxi; I fear the bandits may unexpectedly strike east of the river—Lin and Fu cannot be ignored; troops should be shifted to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Today frontier troops guard only Shaanxi; I fear the rebels may unexpectedly strike east of the river—Lin and Fu cannot be ignored; troops should be shifted to guard them.

sentences.zh: 鄜、延與原州、鎮戎軍，皆當賊衝，而兵屯從寡不均。

translations.literal: Yan and Yan along with Yuanzhou and Zhenrong Army all lie on the enemy's path, yet troop dispositions are uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Yan along with Yuanzhou and Zhenrong Army all lie on the enemy's path, yet troop dispositions are uneven.

sentences.zh: 或寇原州、鎮戎軍，則鄜、延能應援。

translations.literal: If the enemy strikes Yuanzhou and Zhenrong Army, Yan and Yan can reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy strikes Yuanzhou and Zhenrong Army, Yan and Yan can reinforce.

sentences.zh: 陝西屯卒太多，永興為關、隴根本，而戍者不及三千。

translations.literal: Too many garrison troops are stationed in Shaanxi; Yongxing is the root of Guan and Long, yet defenders number fewer than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Too many garrison troops are stationed in Shaanxi; Yongxing is the root of Guan and Long, yet defenders number fewer than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 宜留西戍之兵，壯關中形勢，緩急便於調發。

translations.literal: Western garrison troops should be retained to strengthen Guanzhong's posture and ease emergency dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Western garrison troops should be retained to strengthen Guanzhong's posture and ease emergency dispatch.

sentences.zh: 郡縣備盜不謹，請增尉員，益弓手藉。」

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties are lax in guarding against bandits; he asked to add assistant magistrates and increase archer levies."
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties are lax in guarding against bandits; he asked to add assistant magistrates and increase archer levies."

sentences.zh: 其論利害甚多。

translations.literal: His discussions of advantage and harm were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: His discussions of policy were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 紳與梁適同在兩禁，人以為險詖，故語曰：「草頭木腳，陷人倒卓。」

translations.literal: Shen and Liang Shi were both in the Two Restricted Halls; people thought them treacherous and slanderous, hence the saying: "Grass head and wooden foot—overturn a man and drop him."
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Liang Shi were both in the Two Restricted Halls; people thought them treacherous and slanderous, hence the saying: "Grass head and wooden foot—overturn a man and drop him."

sentences.zh: 子頌，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Song has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Song has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 王洙，字原叔，應天宋城人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhu, style name Yuan Shu, was a native of Songcheng in Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu, courtesy name Yuan Shu, was a native of Songcheng in Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 少聰悟博學，記問過人。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever, broadly learned, and his memory surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was clever and broadly learned, with a memory that surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 初舉進士，與郭稹同保。

translations.literal: When he first entered the jinshi examination, he and Guo Zhi were mutual guarantors.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the jinshi examination, he and Guo Zhi were mutual guarantors.

sentences.zh: 人有告稹冒祖母禫，主司欲脫洙連坐之法，召謂曰：「不保，可易也。」

translations.literal: Someone reported that Zhi had falsely claimed mourning for a step-grandmother; the chief examiner wished to exempt Zhu from joint punishment under the law and summoned him, saying: "If you do not guarantee him, you may change."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Zhi had falsely claimed mourning for a step-grandmother; the chief examiner wished to exempt Zhu from joint punishment and summoned him, saying: "If you do not guarantee him, you may change."

sentences.zh: 洙曰：「保之，不願易。」

translations.literal: Zhu said: "I guarantee him and do not wish to change."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu said: "I guarantee him and will not change."

sentences.zh: 遂與稹俱罷。

translations.literal: Both were therefore disqualified.
translations.idiomatic: Both were therefore disqualified.

sentences.zh: 再舉，中甲科，補舒城縣尉。

translations.literal: On a second attempt he passed in the top grade and was appointed assistant magistrate of Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: On a second attempt he passed in the top grade and was appointed assistant magistrate of Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 坐覆縣民鍾元殺妻不實免官。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for reviewing the case of a county man, Zhong Yuan, who killed his wife—a finding that proved false.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for reviewing the case of a county man, Zhong Yuan, who killed his wife—a finding that proved false.

sentences.zh: 後調富川縣主簿。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to chief clerk of Fuchuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to chief clerk of Fuchuan County.

sentences.zh: 晏殊留守南京，厚遇之，薦為府學教授。

translations.literal: Yan Shu, holding Nanjing, treated him generously and recommended him as professor in the prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu, holding Nanjing, treated him generously and recommended him as professor in the prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 召為國子監說書，改直講。

translations.literal: He was summoned as lecturer in the Directorate of Education and transferred to direct lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as lecturer in the Directorate of Education and transferred to direct lecturer.

sentences.zh: 校《史記》、《漢書》，擢史館檢討、同知太常禮院，為天章閣侍講。

translations.literal: He collated the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han, was promoted to reviser in the Academy of History and concurrent vice-director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and served as lecturer in the Tianzhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He collated the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han, was promoted to reviser in the Academy of History and concurrent vice-director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and served as lecturer in the Tianzhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 專讀寶訓、要言於邇英閣。

translations.literal: He specialized in reading the Precious Instructions and Essential Sayings in the Nearby Excellence Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He specialized in reading the Precious Instructions and Essential Sayings in the Nearby Excellence Hall.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常博士、同管勾國子監，預修《崇文總目》成，遷尚書工部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and co-superintendent of the Directorate of Education; when the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Academy was completed he was moved to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and co-superintendent of the Directorate of Education; when the Comprehensive Catalogue of the Chongwen Academy was completed he was moved to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 修《國朝會要》，加直龍圖閣、權同判太常寺。

translations.literal: While compiling the National Institutions of the Dynasty, he was given direct appointment in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and acting vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: While compiling the National Institutions of the Dynasty, he was given direct appointment in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and acting vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 坐赴進奏院賽神與女妓雜坐，為御史劾奏，黜知濠州，徙襄州。

translations.literal: For attending a spirit festival at the Memorial Memorial Court and sitting mixed with female entertainers, he was impeached by censors, demoted to prefect of Haozhou, and transferred to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For attending a spirit festival at the Memorial Memorial Court and sitting mixed with female entertainers, he was impeached by censors, demoted to prefect of Haozhou, and transferred to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會貝卒叛，州郡皆恟恟，襄佐史請罷教閱士，不聽。

translations.literal: When Bei Zhe rebelled, all prefectures were alarmed; the Xiang assistant Shi asked to stop drilling the troops, but Zhu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Bei Zhe rebelled, all prefectures were alarmed; the Xiang assistant Shi asked to stop drilling the troops, but Zhu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 又請毋給真兵，洙曰：「此正使人不安也。」

translations.literal: He also asked not to issue real troops; Zhu said: "That is precisely what would make people uneasy."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked not to issue real troops; Zhu said: "That is precisely what would make people uneasy."

sentences.zh: 命給庫兵，教閱如常日，人無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: He ordered depot troops issued and drilling continued as on ordinary days; no one dared make an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered depot troops issued and drilling continued as on ordinary days; no one dared make an uproar.

sentences.zh: 徙徐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時京東饑，朝廷議塞商胡，賦楗薪，輸半而罷塞。

translations.literal: At that time eastern Shandong suffered famine; the court debated blocking the Shanghu Canal, levying lock timber, and halting the block after delivering half.
translations.idiomatic: At that time eastern Shandong suffered famine; the court debated blocking the Shanghu Canal, levying lock timber, and halting the block after delivering half.

sentences.zh: 洙命更其餘為穀粟，誘願輸者以餔流民，因募其壯者為兵，得千餘人，盜賊衰息。

translations.literal: Zhu ordered the remainder converted to grain and millet, induced willing donors to feed refugees, and recruited the able-bodied as soldiers—more than a thousand men—and banditry subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu ordered the remainder converted to grain and millet, induced willing donors to feed refugees, and recruited the able-bodied as soldiers—more than a thousand men—and banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 有司上其最，為京東第一，徙亳州。

translations.literal: The offices reported his excellence as first in eastern Shandong, and he was transferred to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The offices reported his excellence as first in eastern Shandong, and he was transferred to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 復為天章閣侍講、史館檢討。

translations.literal: He was again made lecturer in the Tianzhang Pavilion and reviser in the Academy of History.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made lecturer in the Tianzhang Pavilion and reviser in the Academy of History.

sentences.zh: 帝將祀明堂，宋祁言：「明堂制度久不講，洙有《禮》學，願得同具其儀。」

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to sacrifice at the Bright Hall, Song Qi said: "Bright Hall ritual has long gone unstudied; Zhu has learning in the Rites—I wish he may jointly set forth the ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to sacrifice at the Bright Hall, Song Qi said: "Bright Hall ritual has long gone unstudied; Zhu has learning in the Rites—I wish he may jointly set forth the ceremony."

sentences.zh: 詔還洙太常，再遷兵部員外郎，命撰《大饗明堂記》。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Zhu to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was promoted again to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of War and ordered to compose the Record of the Great Offering at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Zhu to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was promoted again to outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of War and ordered to compose the Record of the Great Offering at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 除史館修撰，遷知制誥。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academy compiler and promoted to drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academy compiler and promoted to drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 詔諸儒定雅樂，久未決。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the scholars to fix elegant music, but long no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the scholars to fix court music, but long no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 洙與胡瑗更造鍾磬，而無形制容受之別。

translations.literal: Zhu and Hu Yuan remade bells and chimes but without distinction of form, capacity, and volume.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and Hu Yuan remade bells and chimes but without distinction of form, capacity, and volume.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年，有事於南郊，勸上用新樂，既而議者多非之，卒不復用。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangyou, when the southern suburb ceremony was held, they urged use of the new music; thereafter many debated against it and in the end it was not used again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangyou, when the southern suburb ceremony was held, they urged use of the new music; thereafter many debated against it and in the end it was not used again.

sentences.zh: 夏竦卒，賜諡文獻。

translations.literal: When Xia Song died, the posthumous title Literary Offering was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Song died, the posthumous title Literary Offering was granted.

sentences.zh: 洙當草制，封還其目曰：「臣下不當與僖祖同諡。」

translations.literal: Zhu was to draft the edict; he returned the draft title, saying: "A subject should not share a posthumous title with Ancestor Xi."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was to draft the edict; he returned the draft title, saying: "A subject should not share a posthumous title with Ancestor Xi."

sentences.zh: 因言：「前有司諡王溥為文獻，章得象為文憲，字雖異而音同，皆當改。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Formerly the offices gave Wang Pu the posthumous title Literary Offering and Zhang Dexiang Literary Constitution—the characters differ but the sound is the same; both should be changed."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Formerly the offices gave Wang Pu the posthumous title Literary Offering and Zhang Dexiang Literary Constitution—the characters differ but the sound is the same; both should be changed."

sentences.zh: 於是太常更諡竦文莊，而溥、得象皆易諡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices changed Song's title to Literary Sobriety, and Pu and Dexiang were both retitled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices changed Song's title to Literary Sobriety, and Pu and Dexiang were both retitled.

sentences.zh: 嘗使契丹，至鞾淀。

translations.literal: He once served as envoy to the Khitan, reaching Boot Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as envoy to the Khitan, reaching Boot Lake.

sentences.zh: 契丹令劉六符來伴宴，且言耶律防善畫，向持禮南朝，寫聖容以歸，欲持至館中。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent Liu Liufu to accompany the banquet and said that Yelu Fang was skilled at painting; he had long held ritual toward the Southern Court and painted the sage's likeness to take home, and wished to bring it to the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Liu Liufu to accompany the banquet and said that Yelu Fang was skilled at painting; he had long observed ritual toward the Song court and had painted the emperor's likeness to take home, and wished to bring it to the lodge.

sentences.zh: 洙曰：「此非瞻拜之地也。」

translations.literal: Zhu said: "This is not a place for reverent gazing."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu said: "This is not a place for reverent viewing."

sentences.zh: 六符言恐未得其真，欲遣防再往傳繪，洙力拒之。

translations.literal: Liufu said he feared the likeness was not yet true and wished to send Fang again to copy it; Zhu firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Liufu said he feared the likeness was not yet accurate and wished to send Fang again to paint it; Zhu firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 既而洙以兄子堯臣參知政事，改侍讀學士兼侍講學士。

translations.literal: Soon Zhu's nephew by marriage Yao Chen became Vice Director of the Secretariat; Zhu was changed to reader-in-waiting with concurrent lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu's nephew by marriage Yao Chen became Vice Director of the Secretariat; Zhu was made reader-in-waiting with concurrent lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 罷一學士，換二學士且兼講讀，前此未嘗有也。

translations.literal: One academician was removed and two academicians with concurrent lecture and reading were exchanged—never before had this occurred.
translations.idiomatic: One academician was removed and two academicians with concurrent lecture and reading were appointed—never before had this occurred.

sentences.zh: 是歲，京東、河北秋大稔。

translations.literal: That year the autumn harvest in eastern Shandong and Hebei was very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: That year the autumn harvest in eastern Shandong and Hebei was very abundant.

sentences.zh: 洙言：「近年邊糴，增虛價數倍，雖復稍延日月之期，而終償以實錢及山澤之物，以致三司財用之蹙。

translations.literal: Zhu said: "In recent years border grain purchases have raised fictitious prices several times over; though the term is slightly extended, in the end real money and mountain and marsh goods are paid, causing the Three Departments' finances to tighten.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu said: "In recent years border grain purchases have raised fictitious prices several times over; though payment is slightly deferred, in the end real money and goods from hills and marshes are paid, tightening the Three Departments' finances.

sentences.zh: 請借內藏庫禁錢，乘時和糴京東、河北之粟，以供邊食，可以坐紓便糴之急。」

translations.literal: I ask to borrow forbidden funds from the inner treasury and, seizing the season, purchase grain in eastern Shandong and Hebei to supply frontier food—this can ease the urgent border purchase at a sitting."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to borrow forbidden funds from the inner treasury and, seizing the season, purchase grain in eastern Shandong and Hebei to supply frontier provisions—this can ease the urgent border purchase at a stroke."

sentences.zh: 又言：「近時選諫官、御史，凡執政之臣嘗所薦者，皆不與選。

translations.literal: He also said: "In recent selection of remonstrance officials and censors, all whom chief ministers have once recommended are excluded from selection.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In recent selection of remonstrance officials and censors, all whom chief ministers have once recommended are excluded from selection.

sentences.zh: 且士之飭身勵行，稍為大臣所知，反置而不用，甚可惜也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when scholars discipline themselves and encourage conduct and are slightly known to great ministers, they are instead set aside and not used—how regrettable."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when scholars discipline themselves and are slightly known to great ministers, they are instead set aside—how regrettable."

sentences.zh: 及得疾逾月，帝遣使問：「疾少間否，能起侍經席乎？」

translations.literal: When his illness exceeded a month, the emperor sent an envoy to ask: "Is the illness somewhat better—can you rise to attend the classics lecture?"
translations.idiomatic: When his illness exceeded a month, the emperor sent an envoy to ask: "Is the illness somewhat better—can you rise to attend the classics lecture?"

sentences.zh: 時不能起矣。

translations.literal: By then he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: By then he could not rise.

sentences.zh: 洙泛覽傳記，至圖緯、方技、陰陽、五行、算數、音律、詁訓、篆隸之學，無所不通。

translations.literal: Zhu read widely in biographies; in charts and apocrypha, arts and techniques, yin and yang, the five phases, calculation, pitch pipes, glosses, and seal and clerical scripts—there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu read widely in biographies; in charts and apocrypha, arts and techniques, yin and yang, the five phases, calculation, pitch pipes, glosses, and seal and clerical scripts—there was nothing he did not master.

sentences.zh: 及卒賜諡曰文，御史吳中復言官不應得諡，乃止。

translations.literal: On his death he was granted the posthumous title Literary, but Censor Wu Zhongfu said his office did not warrant a posthumous title, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was granted the posthumous title Literary, but Censor Wu Zhongfu said his office did not warrant a posthumous title, and it was stopped.

sentences.zh: 預修《集韻》、《祖宗故事》、《三朝經武聖略》、《鄉兵制度》，著《易傳》十卷、雜文千有餘篇。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Collected Rhymes, Ancestral Stories, Sacred Military Overview of the Three Reigns, and Militia Institutions, and authored ten fascicles of Commentary on the Changes and more than a thousand miscellaneous essays.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Collected Rhymes, Ancestral Stories, Sacred Military Overview of the Three Reigns, and Militia Institutions, and authored ten juan of Commentary on the Changes and more than a thousand miscellaneous essays.

sentences.zh: 子欽臣。

translations.literal: His son was Qinchen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qinchen.

sentences.zh: 子 欽臣

translations.literal: Son Qinchen
translations.idiomatic: His son Qinchen

sentences.zh: 欽臣，字仲至，清亮有志操，以文贄歐陽修，修器重之。

translations.literal: Qinchen, style name Zhongzhi, was pure and bright with moral purpose; he presented writings to Ouyang Xiu, who greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Qinchen, courtesy name Zhongzhi, was pure and principled; he presented writings to Ouyang Xiu, who greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 用蔭入官，文彥博薦試學士院，賜進士及第。

translations.literal: He entered office by yin privilege; Wen Yanbo recommended him for trial in the Academy and he was granted jinshi rank.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by yin privilege; Wen Yanbo recommended him for trial in the Academy and he was granted jinshi rank.

sentences.zh: 歷陝西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He served as vice transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，為工部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanyou era he was outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanyou era he was outer-court vice-director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 奉使高麗，還，進太僕少卿，遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Goryeo, on his return he was advanced to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs and transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to Goryeo, on his return he was advanced to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Studs and transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 開封尹錢勰入對，哲宗言：「比閱書詔，殊不滿人意，誰可為學士者？」

translations.literal: Kaifeng prefect Qian Xie entered audience; Emperor Zhezong said: "Recently reading edicts, I am quite dissatisfied—who can serve as academician?"
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng prefect Qian Xie entered audience; Emperor Zhezong said: "Recently reading edicts, I am quite dissatisfied—who can serve as academician?"

sentences.zh: 勰以欽臣對。

translations.literal: Xie answered with Qinchen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie answered with Qinchen.

sentences.zh: 哲宗曰：「章惇不喜。」

translations.literal: Zhezong said: "Zhang Dun dislikes him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong said: "Zhang Dun dislikes him."

sentences.zh: 乃以勰為學士，欽臣領開封。

translations.literal: Xie was therefore made academician and Qinchen headed Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was therefore made academician and Qinchen headed Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 改集賢殿修撰、知和州。

translations.literal: He was changed to compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to compiler in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 徙饒州，斥提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Raozhou and dismissed as superintendent of the Taiping View.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Raozhou and dismissed as superintendent of the Taiping View.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復待制、知成德軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong acceded, he was restored to awaiting edict and prefect of Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong acceded, he was restored to awaiting edict and prefect of Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 欽臣平生為文至多，所交盡名士，性嗜古，藏書數萬卷，手自讎正，世稱善本。

translations.literal: Qinchen wrote very many works in his lifetime; his associates were all famous men; he loved antiquity by nature and collected tens of thousands of volumes, collating them by hand—his editions were called fine copies.
translations.idiomatic: Qinchen wrote very many works in his lifetime; his associates were all famous men; he loved antiquity by nature and collected tens of thousands of volumes, collating them by hand—his editions were called fine copies.

sentences.zh: 胥偃，字安道，潭州長沙人。

translations.literal: Xu Yan, style name Andao, was a native of Changsha in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan, courtesy name Andao, was a native of Changsha in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少力學，河東柳開見其所為文曰：「異日必得名天下。」

translations.literal: In youth he studied hard; Liu Kai of Hedong, seeing his writings, said: "Another day you will certainly win fame under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied hard; Liu Kai of Hedong, seeing his writings, said: "Another day you will certainly win fame under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，授大理評事、通判湖、舒二州，直集賢院、同判吏部南曹、知太常禮院，再遷太常丞、知開封縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the top grade and was appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and surveillance commissioner of Hu and Shu prefectures, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, concurrent judge in the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, and director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was promoted again to aide in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Kaifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top grade and was appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and surveillance commissioner of Hu and Shu prefectures, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, concurrent judge in the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, and director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was promoted again to aide in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Kaifeng County.

sentences.zh: 與御史高升試府進士，既封彌卷首，輒發視，擇有名者居上。

translations.literal: With Censor Gao Sheng he tested prefectural jinshi candidates; once the sealed rolls were opened at the head, he would look and place famous men at the top.
translations.idiomatic: With Censor Gao Sheng he tested prefectural jinshi candidates; once the sealed rolls were opened at the head, he would look and place famous men at the top.

sentences.zh: 降秘書省著作佐郎、監光化軍酒。

translations.literal: He was demoted to editorial assistant in the Secretariat and supervisor of wine at Guanghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to editorial assistant in the Secretariat and supervisor of wine at Guanghua Army.

sentences.zh: 起通判鄧州，復太常丞。

translations.literal: He was raised to surveillance commissioner of Dengzhou and restored as aide in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to surveillance commissioner of Dengzhou and restored as aide in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 林特知許州，辟通判州事，徙知漢陽軍。

translations.literal: Lin Te knew Xuzhou and summoned him as surveillance commissioner; he was transferred to military commissioner of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Te knew Xuzhou and summoned him as surveillance commissioner; he was transferred to military commissioner of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 還判三司度支勾院、修起居注。

translations.literal: On return he judged the Three Departments' fiscal verification bureau and revised the Veritable Records.
