sentences.zh: 仁宗命說《尚書》，光輔曰：「堯、舜之事，遠而未易行，願講《無逸》一篇。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong ordered him to expound the Documents; Guangfu said: "The affairs of Yao and Shun are remote and not easy to practice—I pray to expound the chapter 'No Dissipation.'"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong ordered him to expound the Documents; Guangfu said: "The affairs of Yao and Shun are remote and not easy to practice—I pray to expound the chapter 'No Dissipation.'"

sentences.zh: 時年七十餘矣，而論說明暢。

translations.literal: He was then more than seventy, yet his discussion was clear and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then more than seventy, yet his discussion was clear and fluent.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，欲留為學官，固辭，以國子監丞老於家。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and wished to keep him as academic official, but he firmly declined and returned home as aide in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and wished to keep him as academic official, but he firmly declined and returned home as aide in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 安國《五經》及第，為枝江縣尉，後遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Anguo passed the Five Classics examination and served as aide in Zhijiang County, later transferred to aide in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo passed the Five Classics examination and served as aide in Zhijiang County, later transferred to aide in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 光輔教授兗州，請監兗州酒稅，徙監益州糧料院，入為國子監直講，景祐初，置崇政殿說書，安國以國子博士預選。

translations.literal: Guangfu taught in Yanzhou and requested to supervise Yanzhou wine tax; he was transferred to supervise the grain supply office in Yizhou, entered as direct lecturer in the Directorate of Education; in the early Jingyou era the Chongzheng Hall lecture was established and Anguo was selected as erudite in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu taught in Yanzhou and requested to supervise Yanzhou wine tax; he was transferred to supervise the grain supply office in Yizhou, entered as direct lecturer in the Directorate of Education; in the early Jingyou era the Chongzheng Hall lecture was established and Anguo was selected as erudite in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 久之，進天章閣侍講、直龍圖閣，遂為天章閣待制、龍圖閣直學士，皆兼侍講。

translations.literal: After a long while he was advanced to lecturer in the Tianzhang Pavilion and direct appointment in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, then awaiting edict in the Tianzhang Pavilion and direct academician in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion—all with concurrent lecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was advanced to lecturer in the Tianzhang Pavilion and direct appointment in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, then awaiting edict in the Tianzhang Pavilion and direct academician in the Dragon Diagram Pavilion—all with concurrent lecture.

sentences.zh: 進翰林侍講學士，歷判尚書刑部、太常寺，糾察在京刑獄，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy, successively judged the Ministry of Justice and Court of Imperial Sacrifices, investigated capital criminal cases, and was promoted repeatedly to recipient of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy, successively judged the Ministry of Justice and Court of Imperial Sacrifices, investigated capital criminal cases, and was promoted repeatedly to recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒，贈尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At age more than seventy he died and was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At age more than seventy he died and was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安國講說，一以注疏為主，無他發明，引喻鄙俚，世或傳以為笑。

translations.literal: Anguo in lecturing relied solely on commentaries and subcommentaries without other invention; his analogies were vulgar and rustic, and the age sometimes passed them around for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo in lecturing relied solely on commentaries and subcommentaries without other invention; his analogies were vulgar and rustic, and the age sometimes passed them around for laughter.

sentences.zh: 尤喜緯書及注疏所引緯書，則尊之與經等。

translations.literal: He especially loved apocryphal texts and apocryphal texts cited in commentaries, honoring them equally with the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved apocryphal texts and apocryphal texts cited in commentaries, honoring them equally with the classics.

sentences.zh: 在經筵二十七年，仁宗稱其行義淳質，以比先朝崔遵度。

translations.literal: In the classics lecture hall twenty-seven years, Emperor Renzong praised his conduct as pure and simple, comparing him to Cui Zundu of the former court.
translations.idiomatic: In the classics lecture hall twenty-seven years, Emperor Renzong praised his conduct as pure and simple, comparing him to Cui Zundu of the former court.

sentences.zh: 嘗講《易》至《鼎卦》，帝問：「九四象如何？」

translations.literal: He once lectured on the Changes to the Ding hexagram; the emperor asked: "What is the image of the fourth nine?"
translations.idiomatic: He once lectured on the Changes to the Ding hexagram; the emperor asked: "What is the image of the fourth nine?"

sentences.zh: 安國對：「九四上承至尊，上應初爻，行重非據，故折足覆餗。

translations.literal: Anguo answered: "The fourth nine above receives the utmost honored, above it corresponds to the first line—acting with weight without proper footing, therefore the legs break and the stew is overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo answered: "The fourth nine above receives the utmost honored, above it corresponds to the first line—acting with weight without proper footing, therefore the legs break and the stew is overturned.

sentences.zh: 亦猶任得其人，則雖重可勝，非其人，必有顛覆之患。」

translations.literal: It is also like when the appointment fits the man, then though the weight is heavy it can be borne; when the man is not right, there must be the calamity of overturning."
translations.idiomatic: It is also like when the appointment fits the man, then though the weight is heavy it can be borne; when the man is not right, there must be the calamity of overturning."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it as good.

sentences.zh: 又嘗講《周官》至「大荒大劄，則薄征緩刑」，因進言曰：「古所謂緩刑，乃貰過誤之民爾。

translations.literal: He also once lectured on the Offices of Zhou to "great famine and great pestilence—then lighten levies and ease punishments," and therefore advanced saying: "What antiquity called easing punishments was pardoning people who erred through mistake.
translations.idiomatic: He also once lectured on the Offices of Zhou to "great famine and great pestilence—then lighten levies and ease punishments," and therefore advanced saying: "What antiquity called easing punishments was pardoning people who erred through mistake.

sentences.zh: 今眾持兵仗取民廩食，一切寬之，恐無以禁姦。」

translations.literal: Today the multitude bear arms and take the people's granary food—to pardon all alike I fear there will be no means to forbid wickedness."
translations.idiomatic: Today the multitude bear arms and take the people's granary food—to pardon all alike I fear there will be no means to forbid wickedness."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不然，天下皆吾赤子，迫於餓莩。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not so—all under Heaven are my children, driven to banditry by hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Not so—all under Heaven are my children, driven to banditry by hunger.

sentences.zh: 至起為盜。

translations.literal: Only then do they rise as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Only then do they turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 州縣既不能振恤，乃捕而殺之。

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties cannot relieve and support them, they capture and kill them—
translations.idiomatic: When local governments cannot feed and shelter them, they hunt them down and execute them—

sentences.zh: 不亦甚乎。」

translations.literal: is this not excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: can anything be more cruel?"

sentences.zh: 嘗請書《無逸篇》於邇英閣之後屏，帝曰：「朕不欲背聖人之言。」

translations.literal: He once asked to write the chapter "No Dissipation" on the screen behind the Nearby Excellence Hall; the emperor said: "I do not wish to turn my back on the sage's words."
translations.idiomatic: He once asked that the "No Dissipation" chapter be written on the screen behind the Nearby Excellence Hall; the emperor replied: "I do not wish to turn my back on the sage's words."

sentences.zh: 命蔡襄書《無逸》、王洙書《孝經》四章列置左右。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Cai Xiang to write "No Dissipation" and Wang Zhu to write four chapters of the Classic of Filial Piety, arrayed left and right.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then had Cai Xiang write out "No Dissipation" and Wang Zhu write four chapters of the Classic of Filial Piety, displayed on either side.

sentences.zh: 論曰：馮元質直博雅，有古君子之風，歐陽修稱師民醇儒碩學，在仁宗時，並繇宿望，先後執經勸講，庶有所補益矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Feng Yuan was plain, upright, broad, and learned, with the wind of the ancient gentleman; Ouyang Xiu called Shimin a pure Confucian and great scholar—in Emperor Renzong's time both rose by long-standing repute and in succession held the classics and admonished in lecture, and there was some benefit after all.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Feng Yuan was plain, upright, broad, and learned, with the bearing of an ancient gentleman; Ouyang Xiu called Shimin a pure Confucian and great scholar—in Renzong's reign both rose on long-standing repute and lectured on the classics in turn, and the court gained something from them after all.

sentences.zh: 張錫清慎斂晦，晚始見知。

translations.literal: Zhang Xi was clear, cautious, and restrained, and only late was he recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xi was clear-minded, cautious, and self-effacing, and won recognition only late in life.

sentences.zh: 揆及安國父子俱侍經幄，考求其說，亡過人者。

translations.literal: Kui and both Anguo father and son served in the classics curtain; examining their doctrines, there was nothing surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and the Anguo father and son all served in the classics lecture hall; judged by their teaching, none rose above the common run.

sentences.zh: 夫博習修潔之士，潛德隱行，不聞於世者多矣。

translations.literal: Men broadly learned, cultivated, and refined, of hidden virtue and concealed conduct, who are not heard of in the world—how many there are!
translations.idiomatic: How many there are of men broadly learned and self-cultivated, virtuous yet obscure, whom the world never hears of!

sentences.zh: 繇是言之，士遇不遇，豈非命哉！

translations.literal: From this speaking, whether a scholar meets opportunity or not—is it not fate!
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, whether a scholar finds his moment or not—is it not a matter of fate!
